Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant and compliance affidavit filed by the
State-respondent
are taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Devottam Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rajiv Dhar Dwivedi,
learned AGA for the State-respondent.
3.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
104 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Bansdih, District Ballia, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members on 13.3.2022 and according to the FIR on 2.3.2020 marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the sister of the informant and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured her for demand of dowry and on 27.2.2022 wife of the applicant informed the informant about the torture too and subsequently when on 5.3.2022 informant and his family members arrived at the home of the Sonu Singh vs State Of U.P. on 5 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95336133/
1 applicant then found that sister of the informant has been missed.

sentences.text: It is further mentioned in the FIR that it appears that for want of dowry after committing her murder, they concealed her body.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, he has been made accused in the present matter.

6. He further submitted that neither in the FIR nor in the statement recorded during investigation,
any specific demand of dowry could be disclosed and this fact shows that on the basis of vague allegation of demand of dowry, applicant has been made accused in the present matter alongwith his other family members.
7.

He further submitted that actually on 28.2.2022 suddenly wife of the applicant fell ill and she died and as informant side resided in the State of Rajasthan, therefore, after informing them, cremation was conducted and after receiving information, they arrived on 5.3.2022 but inspite of it, on 13.3.2022, FIR of the present case was lodged by the brother of the deceased and this fact suggests that belatedly after consultation, FIR of the present case was lodged.

8. He further submitted that even in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 14.3.2022 i.e. for last more than two and half years and till date, trial of the case, could not be concluded and out of 11 prosecution witnesses only 5 witnesses could be examined and this fact shows that trial of the case is moving with languid pace and there is no hope of its early disposal.

9. He further submitted that family members of the deceased including her parents and brother i.e.
informant of the case have already been examined and there is no chance of tampering of prosecution evidence and applicant is having no criminal history.

10. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within three years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but could not dispute the fact that no specific allegation of demand of dowry could be disclosed either in the FIR or in the statement recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C. of the informant.
However, he further submitted that in haste, without information given to the informant side, cremation of the body of the deceased was conducted by the applicant and his family members.
11. Learned AGA further could not dispute the fact that admittedly, informant side at the time of incident, resided in the State of Rajasthan.
He further could not dispute the fact that however, father of the deceased arrived on 5.3.2022 but in spite of that, FIR of the present case was lodged on 13.3.2022 i.e. after more than a week.

12. He further could not dispute the fact that in the present matter applicant is in jail for last two and half years and till date only five prosecution witnesses could be examined out of 11 prosecution witnesses of the charge sheet.
13. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

sentences.text: From the record, it reflects that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within two years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and record also suggests that without post mortem, dead body of the deceased has been cremated but it reflects that neither in the FIR nor in the statement recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C. informant could disclose any specific demand of dowry
, therefore, this Court finds force in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that on the basis of vague allegations of demand of dowry, FIR of the present case was lodged.

15. Further, as admittedly, at the time of incident, informant side was in the State of Rajasthan,
therefore, it cannot be said that without informing them, cremation of the body of the deceased was conducted by the applicant side.

16. Record further suggests that after receiving information father of the deceased arrived on 5.3.2022 but inspite of that, FIR of the present case was lodged on 13.3.2022 i.e. after more than a week.

17. Further, in the present matter, applicant is in jail since last more than two and half years and till date, only five prosecution witnesses could be examined out of total 11 prosecution witnesses of charge sheet, therefore, there is no hope of early disposal of trial.

18. Record also suggests that family members of the deceased including her parents and her brother i.e. informant of the case have already been examined and therefore, this Court finds merit in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that as all the witnesses of fact have already examined, therefore, there is no chance of tampering with the prosecution evidence.
19.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
20. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

21. Let the applicant -Sonu Singh, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
